extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal funds (K-12 and higher education institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, investigators, and their legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients must handle investigations, evidence production, privacy, and procedural protections in Title IX grievance processes (including interaction with FERPA and State law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to inspect and review evidence directly related to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide both parties an equal opportunity to inspect and review any evidence obtained as part of the investigation that is directly related to the allegations raised in a formal complaint (see §106.45(b)(5)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only evidence 'directly related' to the allegations must be provided; parties must be given time to prepare to respond. The recipient is required to send the evidence to each party and the party's advisor, if any, and allow a minimum ten-day period for written responses after sending the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on access/use of treatment records without voluntary written consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot access, consider, disclose, or otherwise use a party's records made or maintained by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or other recognized professional/paraprofessional acting in that capacity and made/maintained in connection with provision of treatment unless the recipient obtains that party's voluntary, written consent to do so for the grievance process (§106.45(b)(5)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party is not an 'eligible student' under FERPA, the recipient must obtain the voluntary, written consent of a 'parent' as defined in 34 CFR 99.3. Recipients therefore generally will not have access to counseling/therapy/medical records absent consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape-shield limitation on evidence of sexual predisposition/prior sexual behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence about the complainant's sexual predisposition or prior sexual behavior is prohibited unless offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the conduct alleged or to prove consent (§106.45(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such evidence is nonetheless obtained and is directly related to allegations in a formal complaint, the recipient should still allow both parties an equal opportunity to inspect and review it in order to prepare to respond or object to its introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures confidentiality and limited disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures must be offered and may be provided irrespective of filing a formal complaint and are typically confidential under §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures that require mutual cooperation (e.g., mutual restrictions on contact) may necessitate notifying the other party; confidentiality concerns do not prevent required written determinations about grievance results being sent to both parties (but details of remedies need not be disclosed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination content and limits on remedy disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The written determination must state whether remedies will be provided to the complainant but should not state the specific remedies (revised §106.45(b)(7)(ii)(E)). The determination must provide the rationale for the result as to each allegation, including responsibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale must be shared with both parties simultaneously and should provide sufficient basis for appeals (e.g., to reveal unlawful bias). Recipients should not include unnecessary confidential details of remedies (e.g., specific housing changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-retaliation protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must prohibit retaliation; §106.71 expressly prohibits retaliation, including threats, intimidation, and interference with potential witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to participate in a Title IX proceeding is protected; protections apply broadly to deter threats/intimidation and to preserve witnesses' participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and reasonably prompt timeframes for grievance resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must include reasonably prompt timeframes for the conclusion of a grievance process (§106.45(b)(1)(v)). The rule provides a ten-day minimum period for parties to respond in writing after evidence is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although FERPA allows up to 45 days for access to education records, Title IX grievance processes require more prompt timeframes. Recipients must also comply promptly with §106.44(a) obligations (e.g., Title IX Coordinator contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of conflicts between Title IX and FERPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should interpret Title IX and FERPA to avoid conflicts; where a direct conflict exists such that enforcement of FERPA would interfere with Title IX's primary purpose, Title IX requirements override conflicting FERPA provisions (consistent with GEPA and Department Preamble guidance and §106.6(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department administers both statutes and will provide technical assistance; however, whether FERPA applies to a particular record remains a fact-specific determination under FERPA itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA coverage and 'education records' in Title IX investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA defines 'education records' as records directly related to a student and maintained by an institution; evidence directly related to allegations in a formal complaint may constitute education records of both complainant and respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under FERPA, a parent or eligible student generally has the right to inspect witness statements and education records that cannot be segregated/redacted without destroying meaning; Title IX recipients must reconcile this with due process obligations to provide notice and opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction authority and restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with FERPA, recipients may redact personally identifiable information from education records if the information is not directly related to the allegations raised in a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should be judicious and not redact more information than necessary so as to fully comply with §106.45 obligations; Department declined to add more specific redaction rules because existing authorities suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against dissemination of unlawfully obtained recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient knows a recording was unlawfully created under State law, the recipient should not share a copy of such unlawful recording; the Department is not requiring dissemination of illegally obtained evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation's disclosure requirement concerns sharing evidence with the other party to provide notice and opportunity to respond, not wide public dissemination; Department takes no position on state sunshine laws' treatment of Title IX records.

rubrics_metrics.name: IEP/Section 504 and other treatment/education plan records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to release an IEP or Section 504 plan in their possession; if a party offers an IEP/Section 504 plan or consents to its use and it is directly related to allegations, the other party should be able to inspect and review that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment-related records remain protected absent voluntary consent as described in §106.45(b)(5)(i); recipients should consider FERPA and state law implications when handling such documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to determine what is directly related
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have some discretion in determining what evidence is 'directly related' to the allegations raised in a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should exercise judgment when collecting evidence to avoid obtaining and producing irrelevant or overly broad information; however, fear of OCR enforcement may motivate broader collection, which the Department acknowledges as a commenter concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on sharing disciplinary findings with other institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA contains permissive exceptions that may allow disclosure of disciplinary information to another school where a student seeks/enrolls or poses significant risk, but such disclosures are permissive and not mandatory; the Department takes no position requiring recipients to share such information on transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sending school forwards records under FERPA exceptions, it must follow FERPA notice/notification requirements (e.g., annual notification, opportunity to amend, reasonable attempt to notify parent/eligible student).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant rights when Title IX Coordinator signs formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules leave the Title IX Coordinator discretion to sign a formal complaint; if a Coordinator signs against complainant wishes, the complainant remains a party and retains rights (notice of allegations, notice of meetings/interviews, copy of evidence subject to inspection and review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed a prior proposed mandatory requirement that Coordinators must sign in certain circumstances. Recognize practical difficulty obtaining complainant cooperation if Coordinator proceeds over objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of parties' privacy balanced with due process
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations aim to balance privacy concerns with constitutional due process—parties must have notice and meaningful opportunity to respond, while certain private information may be withheld if not directly related or protected by consent/state law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that the rules asymmetrically harm complainants; respondents may also have sensitive records (e.g., criminal investigations). Recipients must navigate FERPA, State law, and Title IX obligations together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on broad public dissemination via production requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is not requiring recipients to widely disseminate public records upon request; disclosure under §106.45 concerns sharing solely with the other party to provide sufficient notice and opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether records generated during Title IX processes become subject to State sunshine laws is a matter of state law and context; recipients should evaluate sunshine law requests based on state-specific rules.
